criterion_notes.c1: Does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access. Coverage figures are presented only as descriptive stylized background in Section 1.5; the empirical study examines the input-oriented technical/productive efficiency of urban water and sanitation utilities (EPS), treating active connections and billed volume as exogenously fixed by demand.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 reading: Under the plain literal wording of Criterion 2, this study PASSES (plain=yes) because Model 2 empirically analyzes regulatory and institutional interventions affecting utilities (months under SUNASS tariff regulation, duration of transitions between tariff formulas, number of SUNASS supervisory inspections/fiscalizaciones, and months under OTASS Transitional Support Regime/RAT administration). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it FAILS (narrow=no) because those regulatory variables are examined only as determinants of utility-level productive/input efficiency, not as rule-type mechanisms directly governing household or community service access. Even under the plain Criterion 2 reading, the study is still excluded (plain_criterion2_decision = exclude) because it fails Criteria 1 and 4 (wrong outcome: utility technical efficiency rather than service access).
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical quantitative panel study (N = 423 utility-year observations across 47 EPS from 2015 to 2023) using two-stage input-oriented VRS Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) followed by Tobit and Simar & Wilson (2007) double-bootstrap truncated regressions.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4 (E04 Wrong outcome): the dependent variable in all second-stage empirical models is utility input-oriented technical efficiency (te_vrs, radial input contraction holding outputs fixed). Active connections, continuity, pressure, billed volume, and wastewater treatment enter only as components of the fixed output vector inside the first-stage DEA efficiency score and are never analyzed as access outcomes of the regulatory variables.
criterion_notes.c5: Unit of analysis/population (balanced panel of 47 urban Peruvian water and sanitation utilities, 2015-2023), environmental and regulatory exposures, technical efficiency outcome, and two-stage DEA econometric design are clearly specified.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with an English abstract (PDF pages 7-8). Per Criterion 10, direct assessment/translation from the provided Spanish full text is feasible (performed directly during screening), though the study is excluded on substantive outcome/scope grounds.

evidence_quotes.quote: This study analyzes the impact of environmental and regulatory variables on the technical efficiency of 47 EPS between 2015 and 2023.

Determinar el impacto de variables ambientales y regulatorias en la eficiencia técnica de las empresas prestadoras de servicios de agua potable y saneamiento (EPS) peruanas (2015-2023), mediante un análisis de DEA en dos etapas.

Se eligió un modelo DEA orientado a insumos bajo el supuesto de rendimientos variables a escala (VRS) debido a la naturaleza de las EPS como monopolios naturales regulados, donde los outputs (conexiones activas, volumen de agua producido y facturado) están determinados exógenamente por la demanda.

Para el caso peruano, considerando su diseño regulatorio, se identificaron tres mecanismos clave: (1) la regulación tarifaria (formulas tarifarias por periodos regulatorios), que incluye fases de transición entre la conclusión de un periodo y el inicio del siguiente; (2) la intervención mediante el Régimen de Apoyo Transitorio (RAT), activado ante situaciones que afectan la sostenibilidad del servicio; y (3) el proceso de fiscalización orientado a verificar el cumplimiento del marco normativo.
El estudio se basa en un panel balanceado de 47 EPS, con información anual correspondiente al periodo 2015–2023.

raw_response.exposure: Environmental variables (macro-region, utility size, number of localities, micrometering percentage, connection density) in Model 1; regulatory variables (months under SUNASS tariff regulation, duration of transitions between tariff formulas, number of SUNASS supervisory inspections/fiscalizaciones, and months under OTASS Transitional Support Regime/RAT) in Model 2
raw_response.outcome: Utility input-oriented VRS technical efficiency score (te_vrs, bounded between 0 and 1)
raw_response.population_and_sample: Balanced panel of 47 urban water and sanitation service provider utilities (Empresas Prestadoras de Servicios de Saneamiento, EPS) in Peru over 2015-2023 (N = 423 utility-year observations; N = 321 inefficient DMUs in Simar & Wilson truncated regressions), excluding Sedapal S.A. and two small EPS with incomplete data
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E04 (Wrong outcome). Although this empirical Master's thesis (in Spanish, with full text directly readable) evaluates regulatory interventions in Peru's urban water and sanitation sector—specifically SUNASS tariff regulation duration, tariff formula transition length, supervisory inspections (fiscalizaciones), and OTASS Transitional Support Regime (RAT) intervention—its dependent variable is exclusively utility-level input-oriented DEA technical efficiency (te_vrs), measuring radial reduction in utility inputs (workers, operating costs, water produced, pipe network length) holding outputs fixed. Service indicators such as active water connections and continuity are used only as exogenous demand-determined outputs inside the first-stage DEA efficiency score and are not modeled as access, connection, continuity, or affordability outcomes of legal or regulatory rules. Accordingly, it fails Criteria 1 and 4 (and fails narrow Criterion 2 because the regulatory variables are not studied as rule-type mechanisms governing household/community service access), yielding exclusion under both the narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings.
raw_response.study_design: Quantitative panel observational study using two-stage input-oriented VRS Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) with second-stage Tobit and Simar & Wilson (2007) double-bootstrap truncated regressions
